newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila seeks accord on seizures at sea.
newsitem.headline: Manila seeks accord on seizures at sea.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos called on Monday for an international convention that would allow the impounding of fishing vessels apprehended in member states' national waters.

Ramos's proposal, at a meeting in this southern city of fishing industry executives from Southeast Asia, follows Manila's recent arrest of 21 Chinese fishermen for allegedly encroaching in its waters.

The Chinese were captured on May 20 off a shoal in the South China Sea which both Manila and Beijing claim. China says everything in this sea historically belongs to it and has demanded the release of the fishermen and their boat.
Ramos told the meeting, organised by the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), that there needed to be an international mechanism "to enforce conservation and management rules on the sea".

"This means granting the authority to states -- other than the flag state of a fishing vessel -- to stop, board, inspect, investigate, detain and prosecute fishing vessels while on the high seas," he said. He did not elaborate.
ASEAN groups the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore and Brunei.

Ramos suggested Filipinos were partly to blame for incidents involving the arrest of Filipino fishermen in neighbouring countries' waters. He said local officials should warn the fishermen "that there is a limit to where they can go".

"Out there, there are no boundaries. The schools of fish don't stay permanently waiting to be caught, and so we must understand the plight of the fishermen who have to work so hard and risk their lives ... to catch the fish need for their three meals a day," he said.
